title: Protect information
summary: Security includes keeping information private, correct and available when needed. These three goals are often called confidentiality, integrity and availability.
introduction: Security includes keeping information private, correct and available when needed. These three goals are often called confidentiality, integrity and availability. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: Security includes keeping information private, correct and available when needed. These three goals are often called confidentiality, integrity and availability.

blocks.title: Before you start
blocks.text: Use only your own practice data. These lessons do not teach attacks against other people's systems and do not require a real account or secret.
This course teaches the basics. It does not cover every feature of Cybersecurity Fundamentals. Keep real personal data and secret keys out of practice files.

blocks.code:
Private: only the teacher sees a private note
Correct: a score is not changed by accident
Available: the lesson page opens when needed
blocks.title: Protect information

blocks.text: Each line protects a different part of using information safely.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Give one example of each goal for a school library.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Protecting privacy alone does not guarantee a service remains usable or correct.
For more detail later, use this [Cybersecurity Fundamentals further reading](https://www.cisa.gov/secure-our-world).
